content: Self-pairing on the pyrimidin-4-yl probe, which at 0.44 was the least bad of the diazines. Atom 0 is its azine methyl over an acyclic bond. I ruled out making the central ring a pyridine on a single measurement - 0.19 against 0.41 - but that test put the ring nitrogen immediately adjacent to the arylamine, which is exactly the kind of position that proved fatal on the azine ring too. So what I actually established is that a nitrogen next to the linkage is bad, not that the central ring has to be a benzene. This episode separates those: a pyridine nitrogen placed meta to both substituents, as far from either N-H as the ring allows. If activity holds, the central ring is only constrained near its attachment points and I gain a free log unit of lipophilicity, which is worth real QED at LogP 4.2. If it collapses again, the benzene requirement is general and I can stop revisiting it. Surviving methyl goes to the azine C4, meta anilide and cyclopropyl cap otherwise unchanged. Expected product: about 284 Da.
